reaction: The explanation made the lining’s purpose clear.
reason: Adding capillaries should bring blood close to the air sacs for exchange.
expectation: I expect air sacs surrounded by pulmonary capillaries, though they may still need connecting to the circulation.

effect: The airways and exchange surfaces now form lungs, ready to connect to the circulation.
reaction: The completed structure is easy to picture, though the result adds little explanation.
reason: This is the only available combination and directly addresses the goal of connecting the lungs to circulating blood.
expectation: I expect the lungs to connect to the pulmonary circulation, completing the goal.

effect: The lungs are connected to the circulation, completing the goal. The result also makes clear that fresh air must keep reaching the sacs for exchange to continue.
reaction: Connecting the completed lungs to the blood loops was satisfying and made their shared purpose clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Wrapping the air sacs in capillaries was most worthwhile: it showed how their closeness supports gas exchange and connected the lung structure to its job.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding elastic support felt least informative. The picture describes where the fibres go, but the result did not explain how elasticity helps breathing.

surprise.text: Surfactant helps keep the sacs from collapsing as they get smaller during breathing; its purpose was clearer after the result.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the reason for adding elastic tissue remained underexplained. The compatible-options menu guided my choices, so I did not discover the combinations myself.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the connected systems support the body, though I would hope for more explanations of what added structures do.
